gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-jp: Noto Sans JP reads tall and open, its curves sweeping wide. Styro hits hardest with its crowded, retro punch up top, while the body does its best work by giving every stroke room to breathe.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-kaithi: Styro pushes its retro, commanding letters tight together, with barely a gap in the e or c shapes. Noto Sans Kaithi simply opens everything back up.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-kannada: Styro is the retro, commanding one, with a sizable lowercase pressed so close it feels crowded. And Noto Sans Kannada is the approachable one, its s curves opening wide at both ends.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-kayah-li: Clean and unfussy, the body lifts its brush ends before curves can close. Styro is strongest when it packs its heavy lowercase tightly for retro punch, whereas Noto Sans Kayah Li is strongest in leaving every shape open.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-kharoshthi: Approachable and contemporary, Noto Sans Kharoshthi never lets a curve close back on itself. Over a full page its thick, dark lowercase builds a steady stripe through every line, which Styro's crowded retro letters then tighten into something more commanding.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-khmer: Tight, retro and a bit bossy. Noto Sans Khmer then opens generous notches like chisel cuts in wood, and that crowded-versus-open split is the strongest thing about the pair.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-khojki: Modern and clean, the body font lets light pass through wide exits and a large eye on every e. Pressed close and retro, Styro is the crowded counterpoint, and that open-versus-closed split is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-khudawadi: Styro's lowercase is sizable and pressed so tight it feels crowded, with barely a gap in its e and c shapes. Noto Sans Khudawadi leaves its rounds unsealed like an unlatched hook, so the two trade tension for openness down the page.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-kr: Contemporary and clean, Noto Sans KR keeps generous gaps in its curves beside a big x-height with stubby ascenders and descenders. Styro's crowded retro letters sit above it as the tight, commanding foil.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-lao: Styro brings a retro, commanding look, its sizable lowercase pressed tight with barely a gap in the e or c. And Noto Sans Lao rises well above the usual x-height, so a slightly smaller body size would still hold its own.
